summary: Applying a gold piece matches C through item selection, then JavaScript refuses apply.c:flip_coin. C describes the coin, drops one if underwater or fingers are slippery (or a low-Dexterity draw fails), otherwise draws rn2(100) when hallucinating or rn2(2) for normal heads/tails. The whole function and doapply coin-class dispatch are missing; dropped-coin branches must preserve splitobj and dropx behavior.

source.branch: For a dry, neither glib nor fumbling, nonhallucinating Wizard with normal Dexterity applying a gold piece, doapply dispatches COIN_CLASS to flip_coin; after the flip message it draws rn2(2) and prints heads or tails. Underwater, Glib/Fumbling and low Dexterity may instead split one coin from a stack and drop it, while hallucination uses a separate rn2(100) branch.
callers: apply.c:doapply dispatches COIN_CLASS to flip_coin at 4240-4241; js/apply.js:doapply currently throws UnsupportedApplyError for COIN_CLASS.
dependencies: invent.c:splitobj returns a separate coin when the stack has quantity above one; do.c:dropx then drops it. Preserve stack and floor state through those consumed and void calls.
fingers_or_gloves and objnam.c:singular/xname determine messages; Glib, Fumbling, Hallucination and ACURR(A_DEX) control C branch/RNG order.

evidence: Saved v10 evaluation challenges/evaluations/20260928083103-v10.json matches 16/17 screens then stops at step 16 on flip_coin refusal, with 2992/3001 RNG calls matched. The C recording SHA-256 is 74a817f2bb295a3ec4019a480f358a4444124cac5e19e3d735a97f21fdf207e0.
Upstream nethack-c/upstream/src/apply.c:4528-4564 defines the full flip_coin function and the normal rn2(2) branch; apply.c:4240-4241 wires the coin class.
js/apply.js:3471-3472 refuses COIN_CLASS; the independent recipe wishes a gold piece and applies it.
